questions.question: Whose 1690 'Essay upon the Ancient and Modern Learning'—which praised the spurious Epistles of Phalaris—prompted Jonathan Swift to write 'The Battle of the Books'?
questions.explanation: Swift served as secretary at Moor Park to Sir William Temple and wrote The Battle of the Books to defend him against Bentley and Wotton.

questions.question: In Jonathan Swift's 'A Tale of a Tub' (1704), what is the persona of the narrator who authors the chaotic prefaces and digressions?
options: M. B. a prosperous linen draper of St. Francis Street in Dublin
Captain Lemuel Gulliver of Redriff in Nottinghamshire
Isaac Bickerstaff the famous astrologer of London
A modern Grub Street hack of the Republic of Letters
questions.explanation: Swift parodies modern pedantry and self-importance by speaking through an impoverished half-mad Grub Street hack.

questions.question: What is the subject of the famous Section IX digression in Jonathan Swift's 'A Tale of a Tub', which attributes conquests and philosophies to vapours rising to the brain?
options: The invention of the printing press
questions.explanation: Section IX is titled A Digression concerning the Original the Use and Improvement of Madness in a Commonwealth.

questions.question: In his 1711 ironic pamphlet 'An Argument Against Abolishing Christianity', what distinction does Swift's speaker draw to reassure readers he seeks no moral reform?
options: High Church orthodoxy versus Low Church dissent
questions.explanation: The speaker argues solely for preserving Nominal Christianity admitting that restoring Real Christianity would ruin trade and politics.

questions.question: In Jonathan Swift's autobiographical poem 'Cadenus and Vanessa' (written 1713, published 1726), the name 'Cadenus' is a Latin anagram of which word?
questions.explanation: Cadenus is an exact anagram of Decanus the Latin word for Dean referring to Swift office as Dean of St Patrick.

questions.question: Who was the real-life young woman whom Jonathan Swift met in London in 1707 and addressed as 'Vanessa' in 'Cadenus and Vanessa'?
questions.explanation: Swift coined the name Vanessa from Van for Esther Vanhomrigh surname and Essa as a pet form of Esther.

questions.question: Jonathan Swift's 'Verses on the Death of Dr. Swift' (written 1731) opens with a reflection on a cynical maxim by which French moralist?
questions.explanation: Swift cites La Rochefoucauld maxim that in the adversity of our best friends we always find something that does not displease us.

questions.question: In Part III, Chapter 5 of 'Gulliver's Travels', what is the very first scientific project Gulliver observes at the Grand Academy of Lagado?
options: Building grand houses from the roof downward to the foundation
Extracting sunbeams out of cucumbers to warm raw summers
Softening marble slabs into comfortable pillows and pincushions
Plowing the ground with hogs by burying acorns six inches deep
questions.explanation: The first projector has spent eight years trying to extract sunbeams from cucumbers and seal them in hermetically closed vials.

questions.question: In Part IV of 'Gulliver's Travels', which generous and humane Portuguese sea captain rescues Gulliver and returns him to Lisbon?
questions.explanation: Don Pedro de Mendez treats the misanthropic Gulliver with patience and charity contrasting with Gulliver disgust for all humanity.

questions.question: In Part III of 'An Essay on Criticism' (1711), which short-tempered contemporary critic did Alexander Pope mock under the name 'Appius'?
questions.explanation: Pope mocked John Dennis tragedy Appius and Virginia in lines describing Appius reddening at each word.

questions.question: In Canto IV of 'The Rape of the Lock', which dusky, melancholy gnome descends to the 'Cave of Spleen' to fetch a bag of sighs and a vial of tears?
questions.explanation: Umbriel a dusky melancholy sprite flies down to the central earth to obtain sorrows and grief from the Queen of Spleen.

questions.question: In Canto II of 'The Rape of the Lock', which sylph is specifically assigned by Ariel to guard Belinda's favorite curl, while Zephyretta guards her fan?
questions.explanation: Ariel assigns Brillante to the drops Momentilla to the watch and Crispissa to Belinda favorite lock.

questions.question: In 'The Rape of the Lock', which fierce amazonian friend of Belinda fans her anger over the lost curl and orders Sir Plume to demand its return?
questions.explanation: Named after the mythical Queen of the Amazons Thalestris urges war over reputation and commands her beau Sir Plume to intervene.

questions.question: In his 'Epistle to Burlington' (Moral Essays IV, 1731), through what fictional country seat does Alexander Pope satirize grandiose, tasteless architecture?
questions.explanation: Pope describes a day spent at Timon Villa where brobdignagian scale and symmetry ignore nature and comfort.

questions.question: To which lifelong friend did Alexander Pope address his 1735 'Epistle to a Lady: Of the Characters of Women' (Moral Essays II)?
questions.explanation: Pope addressed the epistle to his close friend Martha Blount praising her serene temper at the poem conclusion.

questions.question: In his 'Epistle to Cobham' (Moral Essays I, 1734), what psychological concept does Alexander Pope advance as the master clue to human character?
questions.explanation: Pope argues that searching a person Ruling Passion resolves all apparent contradictions in human behavior.

questions.question: By what ironic Roman imperial name did Alexander Pope address King George II in his 1737 'First Epistle of the Second Book of Horace, Imitated'?
questions.explanation: Pope ironically addressed the unliterary King George II whose middle name was Augustus by praising virtues the king lacked.

questions.question: In which consecutive run of eleven issues of 'The Spectator' in June and July 1712 did Joseph Addison publish his essays on the 'Pleasures of the Imagination'?
questions.explanation: Addison published his eleven foundational aesthetic essays on the Great the Uncommon and the Beautiful in Spectator 411 to 421.

questions.question: How did Joseph Addison publish his famous eighteen critical papers examining John Milton's 'Paradise Lost' in 'The Spectator' in 1712?
options: They appeared every Monday for eighteen consecutive weeks
They alternated daily with Steele's papers on Sir Roger de Coverley
They were issued as a single special volume at Christmas 1711
They appeared every Saturday from January to May 1712
questions.explanation: Addison eighteen papers on Paradise Lost ran in consecutive Saturday issues beginning with No 267 on 5 January 1712.

questions.question: In 'The Spectator' Nos. 58–62, Joseph Addison distinguishes between 'True Wit' (resemblance of ideas), 'False Wit' (resemblance of words), and what third category?
questions.explanation: Addison defines Mixed Wit in No 62 as a composition of pun and true wit partly residing in words and partly in ideas.

questions.question: Which fiscal measure enacted by Parliament in August 1712 imposed a tax of a halfpenny per half-sheet on periodicals, hastening the end of the original 'Spectator'?
questions.explanation: The Stamp Act of 1712 doubled the price of The Spectator from one penny to twopence and drove many small papers out of business.

questions.question: Why did Daniel Defoe compose his bestselling 1701 verse satire 'The True-Born Englishman'?
options: To protest the massive immigration of French Huguenot weavers into London
To oppose the proposed parliamentary and commercial union with Scotland
To defend the Dutch-born King William III against xenophobic attacks
To celebrate the purely English lineage and Protestant faith of Princess Anne
questions.explanation: Replying to John Tutchin The Foreigners Defoe showed that the English were a mongrel race descended from Romans Saxons Danes and Normans.

questions.question: Which 1706 pamphlet by Daniel Defoe reports a vivid ghost sighting in Canterbury, famously boosting sales of Charles Drelincourt's book on death?
options: An Essay on the History and Reality of Apparitions
A True Relation of the Apparition of One Mrs. Veal
The Political History of the Devil
questions.explanation: Defoe realistic report of Mrs Veal appearing to Mrs Bargrave the day after her death exemplifies his circumstantial realism.

questions.question: With what initials does Daniel Defoe sign the narrative of the Whitechapel saddler at the conclusion of 'A Journal of the Plague Year' (1722)?
questions.explanation: The narrative is signed H.F. generally identified with Defoe uncle Henry Foe a London saddler who lived through 1665.

questions.question: In Daniel Defoe's 'Roxana' (1724), what is the name of the fiercely devoted maidservant who is strongly implied to have murdered Roxana's daughter Susan?
questions.explanation: Roxana maid Amy acts as her moral double and vanishes after promising to silence Susan who threatens to expose Roxana past.

questions.question: Whose rustic pastorals, printed in Tonson's 1709 'Miscellanies', did Alexander Pope ironically praise in 'The Guardian' No. 40 to expose their absurdity?
questions.explanation: Pope anonymously wrote Guardian No 40 pretending to prefer Ambrose Philips clumsy rustic lines over his own smooth Pastorals.

questions.question: Which 1714 six-part pastoral burlesque did John Gay write at Pope's suggestion, featuring coarse country lovers named Lobbin Clout and Blouzelinda?
questions.explanation: Gay The Shepherd Week in Six Pastorals parodied Ambrose Philips rustic style while offering vivid pictures of rural folklore.

questions.question: Which 1717 theatrical farce featuring the pedantic antiquarian Dr. Fossile was jointly written by John Gay, Alexander Pope, and John Arbuthnot?
questions.explanation: Three Hours after Marriage mocked Dr John Woodward as Fossile and included a famous scene with suitors disguised as a mummy and crocodile.

questions.question: Which three-canto Hudibrastic poem (1718) by Matthew Prior playfully debates the seat of the human soul between the brain and the extremities?
options: Alma: or, The Progress of the Mind
Solomon on the Vanity of the World
questions.explanation: In Alma Prior reconciles Aristotle and Descartes by arguing that the soul enters at the toes in youth and rises to the head in old age.

questions.question: Which Horatian wish-poem published in 1700 by the clergyman John Pomfret was judged by Samuel Johnson to be perhaps the most frequently read poem in English?
questions.explanation: John Pomfret The Choice published in 1700 celebrated a moderate rural life of books modest wealth and quiet friendship.

questions.question: Which 1701 burlesque poem by John Philips initiated the eighteenth-century vogue for Miltonic blank-verse parodies by depicting a penniless debtor in a garret?
questions.explanation: Philips The Splendid Shilling applied grand Miltonic diction and syntax to an impoverished student hiding from a bailiff.

questions.question: Which mock-heroic poem (1699, revised 1706) by the physician Sir Samuel Garth satirized a quarrel between the College of Physicians and the apothecaries?
questions.explanation: Garth The Dispensary modeled on Boileau Le Lutrin was an important link between Dryden Mac Flecknoe and Pope The Rape of the Lock.

questions.question: Which 1726 topographical poem in octosyllabic couplets by the Welsh painter-poet John Dyer celebrates the ruined castle and valley of the River Towy?
questions.explanation: John Dyer published Grongar Hill in 1726 blending picturesque landscape observation with moral meditation.

questions.question: Which 1743 blank-verse poem of nearly 800 lines by the Scottish minister Robert Blair significantly advanced the popularity of the Graveyard School?
questions.explanation: Robert Blair published The Grave in 1743 using Elizabethan dramatic blank verse to meditate on charnel houses and tombs.

questions.question: Which member of the Scriblerus Club and Irish archdeacon authored 'A Night-Piece on Death' (published posthumously by Pope in 1721), an early Graveyard landmark?
questions.explanation: Thomas Parnell died in 1718 and Pope edited his Poems on Several Occasions in 1721 containing A Night-Piece on Death and The Hermit.

questions.question: Which 1725 Scots pastoral comedy in five acts by Allan Ramsay helped inaugurate the eighteenth-century vernacular Scottish literary revival?
questions.explanation: Allan Ramsay The Gentle Shepherd set in the Pentland Hills near Edinburgh became a beloved classic of Scots pastoral drama.

questions.question: Which Whig philosopher published 'Characteristics of Men, Manners, Opinions, Times' in 1711, championing an innate 'moral sense' and natural benevolence?
options: Bernard Mandeville author of The Grumbling Hive
Bishop Joseph Butler author of the Analogy of Religion
Francis Hutcheson of the University of Glasgow
Anthony Ashley Cooper, 3rd Earl of Shaftesbury
questions.explanation: The 3rd Earl of Shaftesbury published Characteristics in 1711 inspiring the cult of sensibility and deistic optimism.

questions.question: In Bishop George Berkeley's 1713 'Three Dialogues', which two philosophical speakers debate material substance, with the second defending immaterialism?
questions.explanation: Hylas whose name comes from the Greek for matter defends materialism while Philonous meaning lover of mind voices Berkeley views.

questions.question: Which 1728 treatise by the Nonjuring divine William Law profoundly influenced both the evangelical revival of the Wesleys and the young Samuel Johnson?
options: A Practical Treatise upon Christian Perfection
A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life
questions.explanation: William Law A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life 1728 used sharp character portraits like Miranda and Flavia to urge total devotion.

questions.question: Which influential Tory and Country-party weekly journal was launched in December 1726 by Nicholas Amhurst, Bolingbroke, and Pulteney to oppose Robert Walpole?
questions.explanation: Edited under the persona Caleb D'Anvers of Gray Inn The Craftsman was the foremost political opposition journal against Walpole.

questions.question: Which weekly Tory periodical did Jonathan Swift write from November 1710 to June 1711 to defend Robert Harley's ministry and attack the Duke of Marlborough?
questions.explanation: Swift wrote thirty-three issues of The Examiner campaigning for peace with France and discrediting the Whig war party.

questions.question: Which prolific Augustan female dramatist authored 'A Bold Stroke for a Wife' (1718), in which Colonel Fainwell must outwit four eccentric guardians?
questions.explanation: Susanna Centlivre wrote nineteen plays including The Busie Body 1709 The Wonder 1714 and A Bold Stroke for a Wife 1718.

questions.question: In Susanna Centlivre's 'A Bold Stroke for a Wife' (1718), what is the religious denomination of the Pennsylvania merchant Simon Pure, whom Colonel Fainwell impersonates?
questions.explanation: Colonel Fainwell disguises himself as the Pennsylvania Quaker preacher Simon Pure giving rise to the phrase the real Simon Pure.

questions.question: In Henry Fielding's burlesque 'The Tragedy of Tragedies; or, The Life and Death of Tom Thumb the Great' (1731), what fate befalls the miniature hero at the end?
options: He is swallowed whole in the street by a red cow
He is carried off above the clouds by a giant eagle
He drowns tragically inside a silver bowl of hot punch
He is crushed beneath the weight of Queen Dollallolla fan
questions.explanation: Before a general slaughter wipes out the entire royal court Noodle announces that Tom Thumb has been swallowed by a red cow.

questions.question: In Samuel Richardson's 'Pamela' (1740), what is the name of the coarse, cruel housekeeper at Mr. B.'s Lincolnshire estate who holds Pamela captive?
questions.explanation: Unlike the kindly Bedfordshire housekeeper Mrs Jervis the Lincolnshire housekeeper Mrs Jewkes serves as Pamela jailer.

questions.question: In Henry Fielding's 'Joseph Andrews' (1742), what precious possession does the absent-minded Parson Abraham Adams travel toward London to sell, having left it at home?
options: A rare annotated Greek manuscript of the plays of Aeschylus
A complete Latin critical commentary on Homer Iliad
A lengthy theological treatise against the vanity of riches
Nine volumes of his own handwritten sermons
questions.explanation: Parson Adams sets out to sell nine volumes of sermons to a London bookseller but Mrs Adams forgot to pack them in his saddlebags.

questions.question: Whose turbulent life in Grub Street—marked by a homicide trial and his claim to be the cast-off son of Lady Macclesfield—did Samuel Johnson recount in a 1744 biography?
questions.explanation: Johnson published An Account of the Life of Mr Richard Savage in February 1744 a milestone in sympathetic literary biography.

questions.question: Which 1744 three-book blank-verse philosophical poem by the physician Mark Akenside versified Joseph Addison's aesthetic theories of the sublime, wonderful, and fair?
questions.explanation: Mark Akenside published The Pleasures of Imagination in 1744 blending Addisonian aesthetics with Shaftesburian philosophy.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Augustan Age (1700–1745) is NOT correct?
options: The Theatrical Licensing Act of 1737 placed London stage plays under the Lord Chamberlain
The Statute of Anne in 1710 enacted the first statutory copyright law in Great Britain
Jonathan Swift served as Dean of St. Patrick Cathedral in Dublin from 1713 to 1745
Alexander Pope served two terms as Poet Laureate under George I and George II
questions.explanation: As a Roman Catholic Alexander Pope was barred from holding any public office including the Poet Laureateship.

questions.question: Which of the following character-and-work pairings from the Augustan Age (1700–1745) is NOT correctly matched?
options: George Barnwell — Richard Steele's 'The Conscious Lovers'
Lemuel Gulliver — Jonathan Swift's 'Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World'
Belinda — Alexander Pope's 'The Rape of the Lock'
Parson Abraham Adams — Henry Fielding's 'Joseph Andrews'
questions.explanation: George Barnwell is the tragic apprentice in George Lillo 1731 play The London Merchant whereas Young Bevil is the hero of The Conscious Lovers.
